stemMd: An archivist writes: Records of household purchases survive mainly from wealthy families because their accounts were stored in durable bindings. The scarcity of poorer households in the archive therefore says more about preservation than about whether those households bought goods. What is the passage's main caution?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Surviving records may not represent the population that originally produced records.

options.label: C
options.textMd: All historical records should be discarded.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Durable bindings make every record accurate.

explanationMd: The author separates the surviving sample from the original population. Unequal preservation can explain absence, so lack of surviving evidence should not automatically be read as absence of activity.

distractorRationale.d: Their preserved accounts are the basis of the passage.
distractorRationale.a: The passage explicitly warns against this inference.
distractorRationale.c: The author urges caution, not abandonment.
distractorRationale.e: Preservation is not the same as factual accuracy.
